summary: Extends deterministic compile-time diagrams with layered flows, optional subsystem groups, connection kinds, legends, node detail lines, ordered call sequences, and a written-out diagram description.

evidence.sourceGrammar: The registry owns flow and sequence forms, one-to-twenty flow nodes, up to forty flow edges, up to five non-empty groups around some nodes with other nodes beside them, auto/down/right/orthogonal default flow view (layout, with direction as its older spelling), four connection kinds, an optional node detail line, at most one legend and up to eight legend items, two-to-six sequence participants, and one-to-forty labelled ordered messages. Unknown identities, duplicates, empty groups, undeclared groups, sequence direction or layout, layout together with direction, flow self-connections, legend items naming both or neither subject, node legend items without a label, hidden items with a label, duplicate legend items, and bounds fail at authored directives; a sequence message to its own participant is a step drawn as a loop.
evidence.executionCapabilities: Validated records become package-owned deterministic SVG geometry after sanitization. Flow layers come from package code; node order, coordinates, clusters, and label places come from dagre for the two layered views and from ELK for the right-angle view, both at build time; sequences use authored participant and message order. No source string becomes executable syntax or a general graph program.
evidence.confinement: Groups, participants, nodes, edges, labels, and messages are ordinary bounded directive attributes and cause no filesystem lookup or resource resolution beyond the existing Markdown source graph.
evidence.offlineBehavior: Compilation and both file-URL output formats use local package code, the build-time dagre and ELK layout libraries, and CSS only. No visualization server, browser renderer, worker, font request, or network request is required, and no layout code ships to the browser.
evidence.deterministicSerialization: View boxes, layers, node positions, group boxes, routes, labels, legend entries, IDs, descriptions, and output bytes derive only from validated authored order and package constants; the layout candidates are tried in a fixed order and ties keep the earlier one. No clock, randomness, environment locale, viewport measurement, or runtime layout feeds serialization.
evidence.cspAndRuntime: The extension adds SVG elements, package classes, and a tab list that reuses the package tabs runtime to switch compile-time views; it adds no JavaScript controller of its own, inline handler, author CSS, raw HTML, URL, eval, dynamic import, canvas, iframe, or CSP source. Print CSS shows only the author's default view. Existing page theme controls only package variables.
evidence.accessibility: Each diagram remains one labelled atomic image. Its description is written text: node and layer count, groups with members, layers in flow order, connections along the flow and backward connections separately in the legend's words, or every sequence participant and ordered message. The same text is repeated under the picture in a closed native disclosure. Visible node and connection labels wrap rather than truncate, and the description always carries the complete data.
evidence.byteAndPerformanceBudgets: Validation and layout are finite at registry-owned bounds; flow layout runs a fixed number of dagre candidates per layered view and one ELK layout at build time. Every flow ships three views, so its SVG bytes grow by that factor. Rendering adds no listener, observer, timer, animation, network work, or per-frame computation beyond the existing tabs runtime; SVG and description bytes remain covered by compiler accounting and package checks.
evidence.packageDependenciesAndLicenses: Adds @dagrejs/dagre 3.1.1 and its dependency @dagrejs/graphlib 4.0.5, both MIT, and elkjs 0.12.0, dual-licensed EPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0 and used under EPL-2.0, all only at build time for flow layout; elkjs has no runtime dependencies. Charts, sequences, and timelines keep the project-owned registry, validator, HAST/SVG renderer, and CSS.
evidence.compatibility: Existing flow sources build unchanged within source-contract major 1 but are laid out by layers: direction defaults to auto, row is a flow-layer hint, route is a layout pull, and a single group or ungrouped nodes beside groups are ordinary flows without a warning. Sequence, theme, output-format, CLI, ESM, CSP, and review contracts are preserved; every unsupported shape fails instead of invoking a compatibility fallback.
